recipes.name: Pan-Roasted Chicken with Lemon-Garlic Brussels Sprouts and Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
Place bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned but still soft, about 5 minutes. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate. Set aside.
Coat a large baking dish or cast iron skillet with 1 tablespoon olive oil. Arrange lemon slices in a single layer on the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
Stir together remaining 5 tablespoons olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, kosher salt, and black pepper in a large bowl until marinade is well combined.

Add Brussels sprouts to marinade in the bowl; toss until evenly coated. Use a slotted spoon to place Brussels sprouts over lemon slices in the baking dish, draining excess marinade back into the bowl. Scatter cooked bacon over Brussels sprouts.

Add potatoes to remaining marinade in the bowl; toss until evenly coated. Use a slotted spoon to arrange potatoes along the inside edge of the baking dish, draining excess marinade back into the bowl.
Add chicken breast halves to remaining marinade in the bowl; coat thoroughly. Place chicken, skin-side up, over vegetables in the baking dish. Pour any remaining marinade over chicken.

Bake in the preheated oven until chicken is no longer pink at the bone and the juices run clear, about 1 hour. An instant-read thermometer inserted near the bone should read 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Pan-Roasted Chicken with Lemon-Garlic Brussels Sprouts and Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: This lemon chicken with Brussels sprouts is a one-pan meal featuring bone-in, skin-on chicken breasts roasted over garlicky veggies and baby potatoes.

video.description: Lemon, garlic, bacon, sprouts, chicken, and potatoes. Say no more! We'll show you how to make this one-pan meal that's bright in citrus flavor and perfectly satisfying in every way. Ready to serve a hungry crowd in less than 90 minutes.

review.reviewBody: This was good! My husband loved it. Though I must admit that I really braised the chicken, brussel sprouts and potatoes instead of pan roasting. After cooking the bacon, I browned the chicken breasts in the bacon drippings. Then I added about a tablespoon of olive oil to the pan to saute the garlic and added the brussel sprouts, potatoes, lemon juice and salt and pepper. Then I added a little chicken broth and returned the chicken to the pan. I covered it and put it in the oven to cook at 350 for about 40 minutes and it was perfect. Maybe next time I'll actually pan roast it with the lemon slices. I'm sure it is excellent. Thank you LAMBR for sharing this recipe.

I did as the other reviewer said and braised it. 

- Browned bacon and removed. 
- Browned boneless chicken chicken and removed. 
- Browned garlic with 1 T olive oil. 
- Added brussel sprouts back in and tossed. 
- Added Sweet potatoes diced since I had no regular potatoes 
- Added lemon juice, salt pepper as per recipe. 
- Put bacon on top. 
- Added chicken back in. 
- Added 2 c chicken stock. Next time I might do less. 
- Braised for 35 minutes

Sauce was awesome! and everybody ate it surprise dhow much they liked the brussel spouts. A definite repeat!
I used a navel orange instead of lemon. Also boneless, skinless chicken thighs. Added balsamic vinegar to marinade and baby carrots to veggies. Cast iron skillet in a 400 F oven 50 - 60 minutes.

Was a hit with the men in our house. Did not have red potatoes so used russet worked great. Had to use home canned chicken so I put it in the oven minus the chicken for 20 min covered with foil. Put chicken (shredded) on top and cooked for another 20 min. Was great

First, I browned chicken thighs in a pan w/ olive oil, then removed to a baking dish after about 10 min. I added some sweet vermouth, and parsley to the drippings/ oli to make a sauce. I par-boiled the sprouts before adding to the Baking dish too. Then I sliced about 1/2 pkg. of mushrooms and added that to the dish. Put it into a 425 oven and loosely covered w/ foil for 45 min. Absolutely delish! Will cook tihs again,
Thanks for the idea!

Delicious! Based on other reviews, I omitted the sliced lemon and doubled the brussels sprouts. I also used boneless, skinless chicken breasts (and therefore reduced the cooking time and temperature slightly). It was perfect -- definitely a keeper!

I had no problem with the lemons burning though I also braised the chicken thighs first so I only cooked my for 45 minutes. I added green beans, sautéed mushrooms with shallots in a splash of wine and also used 1 pound of Brussels sprouts.

I made this for the first time tonight after saving it to favorites months ago. My husband gave it a 10 and said it looked like a gourmet meal. My 18-year-old son, who has the palate of a toddler, gave it a thumbs up and even ate the Brussels sprouts. The only thing I changed was followed reviews of others and braised the Brussels sprouts in the bacon grease. I also used Meyer lemon cut very thin to line the bottom of the pan. The lemon was not overpowering or acidic as some other reviewers commented. Oh, and definitely double the Brussels sprouts! This is absolutely going into my dinner rotation.

This is delicious! I made a couple of changes - my husband does not like brussels sprouts so I used broccoli. I did not put the lemons on the bottom and I made an extra batch of the sauce to pour over everything before I put it in the oven. I used boneless breasts and the broccoli so I set the oven on 400 instead of 450 and it only took about 40 minutes. 

I will definitely make it again and will try braising everything before putting it in the oven next time. I think I will then cut the temperature to 375 for the 40 minutes.

I loved this! Husband and the kids not so much fans of the Brussel sprouts. Don't use two lemons even if you use more chicken. In this case more is not better ;-) not a good weeknight meal. Next time I may try broccoli and make this on a Sunday. Oh and I braised the veggies and the chicken in the bacon grease before loading in the oven pan.

I wanted to try something new that would appeal to the entire family, from my 92 year old father to my 6 year old grandson. It was a hit! The only substitution I made was thighs rather than chicken breasts, because the store was out of breasts. The sliced lemons lining the bottom of the pan cooked down nicely and I just ate the rinds along with the brussels sprouts. Other reviews complained about the potatoes not cooking. I used baby red potatoes and cut them in half, making them cook fairly quickly. All in all, this dish was a success! I expect that it will become something of a regular at our house.

I just popped my pan on the oven, and I substituted carrots for the brussels and added fresh peppers and onions. Oh! I added orange slices to the pan, just a splash of soy sauce, and a dash of sage to the marinade. The seasoning is on point. Just make it work for you. Another cook took the recipe and made it their own. I think I'll try their version (pan-searing and finishing in the oven...sounds bomb!) Some people complained that the timing didn't allow for the ingredients to cook properly. Maybe next time you'll put the chicken in first in one pan then transfer it to the pan with the uncooked vegetables. Happy cooking!
Seriously, 450 for 60 minutes will produce seriously dry chicken. I tried 400 for 45 minutes…still dry. Recipe should be revisited
We didn’t love this recipe. It wasn’t quite as flavorful as I had hoped, except for the lemon. It sounded really good but for us, this will be a pass in the future.
Flavor was just ok - wayyyyy too much EVOO

Great! It was a hit with everyone. Teenage grandson said it looked like random things put together, as he went for seconds. Awesome "random" things. 
Thank you

I followed the directions---almost , except I used 1 lb. of Brussels sprouts. It was dry, I would double the liquid part. Net time I'll add some chicken broth. 
Also, I had rotisserie chicken from Costco and used that. Next time I'll add the rotisserie chicken at the end just to heat it. Flavor was good. I'll make it again.
I used thighs instead of breast, tasted great!
The dish tastes good, but prep time is not 15 min.

I tripled the oil lemon and garlic as I doubled the sprouts and potatoes. I also had very large chicken breasts. I did mine in a large glass pan. The bacon, lemon and garlic smells like heaven in my home. It was a family favorite and definitely had Greek undertones. Would pair well with nan bread and a glass of white wine.
